\[ y = \sqrt{1 - \left( \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \right)^2} = \sqrt{1 - \frac{1}{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{2}} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}. \]
So, one point is \( \left( \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}, \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \right) \). The value of \( |x| + |y| \) at this point is:
\[ \left| \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \right| + \left| \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \right| = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} = \sqrt{2}. \]

To confirm that this is the maximum, we can check the value at the other points where \( x \) and \( y \) are both negative. The points are \( \left( -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}, -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \right) \) and \( \left( -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}, \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \right) \). At these points, the value of \( |x| + |y| \) is also \( \sqrt{2} \).

Therefore, the largest possible value of \( |x| + |y| \) is \( \boxed{\sqrt{2}} \).
